_readme: Which operator steps in Hand-work a machine could do, and which a person must (DRE-8650). Read by scripts/operator_step_kind.py, whose classify(title, description) the hygiene lane scripts/hygiene_hand_step.py uses to label each Hand-work operator step hand-step:machine or hand-step:person. It only marks the card: the operator still does every step, and nothing is dispatched because of a class. Every phrase is matched case-insensitively as a whole phrase in the card's title or description — never inside a longer word, with any run of whitespace inside it, and only as it is written: `deploys` and `deployed` are not `deploy`, which errs toward a person — add an inflection as its own phrase. Precedence: a `person` phrase anywhere wins, because a card with one person step cannot be finished by a machine; otherwise the FIRST kind in `kinds` with a phrase in the text wins; with no match the card is a person's, which never claims more automation than exists. The person phrases name a person acting, never a thing that merely mentions signing in — a bare `sign-in` is not one, so `Restamp the sign-in pages` is a machine step. `kinds` is ordered narrowest first: a variable is set by a deploy and a Linear card is filed by a person's hand, so a card that names both is the narrower step — DRE-7328's `bootstrap deploy sets a relay environment variable` is a `variable`. Adding a phrase is a reviewed pull request; tests/test_operator_step_kind.py holds the live cards the CEO named on 2026-11-01.

kinds.why: A repository, organization or environment variable set to a named value.
An administrative act in Linear: a project or Initiative archived, a card filed.
A pull request opened for its own sake — a throwaway, a draft or a control a bot could open.
A deploy, a rollout or a restamp of something already merged.
A script run from a checkout.
